findings.title: Untrusted comment body is injected into the DOM via innerHTML
findings.evidence: The renderer now assigns the raw comment body to innerHTML, which parses and executes attacker-supplied markup instead of displaying it as text. Any user-controlled comment containing HTML or event-handler attributes can run script in the page context when rendered.
findings.recommendation: Do not use innerHTML for untrusted comment content. Restore textContent, or sanitize the HTML with a well-reviewed sanitizer before assigning to innerHTML if rich-text comments are explicitly required.
